resolutions.researcher_notes: Shana (official NIOC news, 2024) describes IGAT-9 sections still 'under construction' (Bidboland-Ahvaz section still under construction). World Pipelines (2020) lists it as an upcoming/under-construction trunkline with a projected 2022 start. Two independent outlets support 'construction'. Supersedes the two dead current_refs (iclg / energypress).

World Pipelines (Jan 2020) explicitly gives IGAT-9 an expected start of 2022 (matches StartYear1=2022). Note: this was a projection; per Shana the line was still under construction into 2024/2025, so the 2022 start was not achieved. Single strong source for the projected year -> medium.

Offshore Energy states IGAT-9 adds 110 million cubic meters/day. 110 MMcm/d = ~3,885 MMcf/d (x35.31), which matches Capacity=3885.00 MMcf/d exactly. 110 mcm/d is the widely reported design capacity; only offshore-energy verified as raw text (Financial Tribune capacity article is JS-rendered, nrgedge 403), so medium.

CONTRADICTION: GEM LengthKnown=1,900 km is higher than every located source. Offshore Energy and Shana both give 1,800 km; World Pipelines gives 1,863 km. contains_value=false because none state 1,900. Recommend GEM review length toward ~1,800-1,873 km. Refs added document the length range.
Both Shana (56-inch mainline) and Offshore Energy (56-inch project) confirm the 56 in mainline diameter; matches Diameter=56. Two independent outlets -> high. Supersedes dead ghods-niroo current_ref.

Both Shana articles state the line carries South Pars gas from the Assaluyeh onshore refineries (matches FuelSource='South Pars gas field'). Corroborated in substance by Offshore Energy (Assaluyeh origin = South Pars processing hub). Both explicit refs are Shana (same outlet), so independent=false -> medium.

Shana confirms both endpoints: Assaluyeh origin and Bazargan border crossing in West Azarbaijan Province (matches StartLocation=Asaluyeh, EndLocation=Bazargan, EndState=West Azerbaijan). Offshore Energy independently confirms Assaluyeh origin routed through western provinces to Turkey's border. Two independent -> high.

CONTRADICTION: GEM SegmentCost=8,900,000,000 USD (2014). Two independent 2014 sources (Shana and Offshore Energy) both put NIGC's planned investment at 8.5 billion USD, not 8.9 billion. contains_value=false (no source states 8.9B). Recommend GEM correct to 8.5 billion USD (2014). Refs added document the cost.

World Pipelines states National Iranian Gas Co. owns a 100% equity stake and is the operator; Shana names NIGC as owner/developer. NIGC is wholly state-owned under the Ministry of Petroleum, so GEM's Owner1='Iran Ministry of Petroleum' (100%) is the parent entity -- consistent. Attribution note: direct owner reported as NIGC; reviewer may prefer NIGC over the parent ministry.
